notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue with the precincts that vote on it, checked against the Board's precinct sample ballots (which give the full ballot wording; where the two differ, the ballots are followed).

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
The Board's notice and sample ballots do not give local issue numbers; see your sample ballot for the order.

Court of Appeals: Peter B. Abele (Republican) is still printed on the main ballot for the 4th District seat; the Board's notice marks him deceased (no longer valid), and a supplemental 4th District Court of Appeals ballot lists Jayme Hartley Fountain (Republican) and Todd L. Grace (Democratic). The supplemental ballot is shown here.

issues.title: Proposed zoning plan for the unincorporated area of Monroe Township
issues.text: Shall the zoning plan for the unincorporated area of the Township of Monroe as adopted by the Township of Monroe be approved? (A resolution enacted under Section 519 of the Ohio Revised Code, titled "Monroe Township Zoning Resolution", governing the unincorporated area of Monroe Township, Adams County, Ohio, to preserve the rural and agricultural character of the Township, protect public health, safety, and general welfare, allow reasonable use of property with minimal unnecessary regulation, provide a predictable process for review of higher-impact development, ensure that uses with potentially significant impacts are evaluated and reasonably mitigated, and to promote orderly and compatible land use consistent with Township infrastructure and services; for the purpose of protecting agricultural, residential, and small-scale uses; preventing unreasonable burdens on roads, infrastructure, and public services; providing uniform and objective standards for land use review; and to carry out zoning authority in a manner consistent with Ohio law.)
issues.note: Voting FOR approves the township's zoning resolution; voting AGAINST rejects it.
